# Shiny App

## General Explanation

This app illustrates the Beta Item Response Model (BIRM) with and without response styles (RS). It allows you to visualize how different parameters affect the probability density function of the model. The app is divided into several tabs, each focusing on a specific aspect of the BIRM and response styles.

The Beta Item Response Model with Response Styles (BIRM-RS) and its evaluation in a simulation study and an empirical illustration are described in [Vollbracht et al. (2026)](#sec-reference). The app was developed as a supplement to this paper.

## The Model

In the BIRM, a response $Y_{ij}$ between 0 and 1 follows a beta distribution with shape parameters $m_{ij}$ and $n_{ij}$. The BIRM-RS adds two person parameters for response styles. Both shape parameters depend on the same term:

$$
z_{ij} = \exp(\eta^{ERS}_i) \cdot (\theta_i - \delta_j + x_j \cdot \eta^{ARS}_i),
$$

$$
Y_{ij} \sim \text{Beta}(m_{ij}, n_{ij}), \quad
m_{ij} = \exp\left(\frac{z_{ij} + \tau_j}{2}\right), \quad
n_{ij} = \exp\left(\frac{-z_{ij} + \tau_j}{2}\right).
$$

Here, $\theta_i$ is the trait of person $i$, $\delta_j$ the difficulty of item $j$, $\tau_j$ its dispersion parameter, and $x_j$ is $1$ for regular and $-1$ for reverse-scored items. The expected response is $\text{logit}^{-1}(z_{ij})$. The ERS parameter $\eta^{ERS}_i$ stretches the distance between trait and item difficulty, so that responses move toward the end that the trait favors. Negative values shrink the distance and move responses toward the center (midpoint response style). ERS and MRS are thus the two poles of one dimension. The ARS parameter $\eta^{ARS}_i$ shifts responses toward agreement. Because this shift reverses with the item direction, reverse-scored items are needed to separate ARS from the trait. With $\eta^{ERS}_i = \eta^{ARS}_i = 0$, the model reduces to the BIRM of [Noel & Dauvier (2007)](#sec-reference).

The probability density functions represent the distribution of responses for a given person–item combination, denoted by the indices $i$ (person) and $j$ (item).

## Tabs

**Standard Beta**: Displays the probability density function of a standard beta distribution with shape parameters $m_{ij}$ and $n_{ij}$. This visualization helps illustrate the fundamental properties of beta distributions. The beta distribution is defined on the interval [0, 1], making it well-suited for modeling bounded continuous data, such as responses on slider scales.

**BIRM**: Illustrates the original Beta Item Response Model (BIRM) with person parameters ($\theta_i$) and item parameters ($\delta_j$, $\tau_j$). This tab allows you to explore how these parameters influence the probability density function for a given set of parameters. This is the base model proposed by [Noel & Dauvier (2007)](#sec-reference), which we extend in the subsequent tabs.

**ERS only**: Shows the BIRM with an additional extreme response style (ERS) parameter ($\eta^{ERS}_{i}$). This tab allows you to examine how ERS influences the shape and location of the probability density function.

**ARS only**: Displays the BIRM with an acquiescence response style (ARS) parameter ($\eta^{ARS}_{i}$) and effect-coded item direction ($x_j$). This tab visualizes how both the ARS parameter and item direction affect the probability density function.

**BIRM-RS**: Combines both ERS and ARS parameters in the BIRM. This tab enables you to explore the joint influence of these two response styles on the probability density function.

**BIRM-RS Simulation**: Simulates sample data based on the full BIRM-RS model. It generates random values for the person parameters ($\theta_i$, $\eta^{ERS}_{i}$, $\eta^{ARS}_{i}$), draws one response per person to an item with the chosen item parameters ($\delta_j$, $\tau_j$), and shows the share of responses in bins of .05. The number of persons can be changed, and a button draws a new sample. This simulation is useful for understanding the model’s behavior across a sample.

In the tabs with response styles, a grey dashed line shows the same person (or, in the simulation, the same persons) without response styles. It can be switched off below the sliders.

## App

*It can take a few seconds (around 10s-30s) to load the app, please be patient.*

```{=html}
<button id="fullscreen-btn" class="btn btn-primary" type="button">Show the app in full screen</button>
<script>
// Hide the button where full screen is not available for page elements (e.g., iPhones)
if (!document.fullscreenEnabled && !document.webkitFullscreenEnabled) {
  document.getElementById("fullscreen-btn").style.display = "none";
}
document.getElementById("fullscreen-btn").addEventListener("click", function () {
  const app = document.querySelector("div.shinylive-wrapper");
  if (!app) return;
  if (app.requestFullscreen) {
    app.requestFullscreen();
  } else if (app.webkitRequestFullscreen) {
    app.webkitRequestFullscreen();
  }
});
</script>
<style>
div.shinylive-wrapper:fullscreen {
  background-color: white;
  overflow: auto;
  margin: 0;
}
div.shinylive-wrapper:fullscreen iframe.app-frame {
  height: 100vh !important;
}
</style>
```
